messages:
erica: noticing a perf regression on paged-attn after the kernel-picker change Friday. latency p50 up ~12% on long context workloads (8k+). saw more frequent small GPU allocations and occasional OOMs :grimacing:

sam: ugh. what changed in the picker? fallback ordering or workspace sizing?

miko: we switched to prefer the fused-kv kernel for seq>1024 which uses a different workspace layout + alloc pattern. profiler shows many short-lived buffers created per-block.

erica: attaching a short snippet from the perf run:
```
ProfilerSummary: blocks_alloc_count=1.2M, avg_block_bytes=48KB, compaction_runs=9.8K, compaction_time_ms=7200, cuda_ooms=3
KernelPicker: selected=fused_kv_v2 for 70% requests (was 18%)
```

oliver: compaction_time 7.2s is... bad. that explains p50. is the block manager trying to compact to satisfy many small allocations?

miko: yes. block size is 64KB right now. lots of reuse churn when requests create 3-5 ephemeral buffers per token. compaction locks the arena for each run.

sam: could we try bumping block size to 256KB for the fused path only? fewer fragments -> less compaction, at cost of a bit more internal slack.

erica: also KV cache behavior: older streams with many short requests cause many tiny prefix caches. those are allocated from the same heap. need to verify if cache pinning is preventing reuse.

oliver: quick experiment idea: add a kernel-specific allocator override in runtime config:
```yaml
block_manager:
  overrides:
    fused_kv_v2:
      min_block_bytes: 256KB
      coalesce_threshold: 0.25 # allow 25% slack before splitting
      max_fragment_age_ms: 1500
```
run this on a canary and check compaction_time + avg_block_bytes.

miko: +1. I can build a canary image. will also enable per-stream alloc tracing to see how KV cache allocations correlate. small pprof script: `runtime --profile=allocs --filter=paged-attn` should capture it.

erica: logged a reproducer: sequence length 8192, batch size 8, sampling topk=40. sends to canary queue now.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/fused-blocktester -> image: gcr.redwood/canary:2026-03-17-fused-blockfix-1 (triggered by miko) :rocket:

sam: if compaction is the hotspot we might also try adaptive reuse: when fragmentation ratio > 0.6, prefer large-new-block allocation instead of compact+split. reduces compaction runs at expense of memory growth.

miko: will add a flag `allocator.aggressive_reuse=true` for testing. also instrument compaction lock contention metric.

oliver: one more angle — the kernel change increased peak workspace requirement by ~30% in telemetry. if the runtime picks fused_kv_v2 but the host doesn't reserve extra workspace, we hit temporary OOMs and then compaction thrashes. maybe kernel picker should expose estimated_workspace_bytes and the router should prefer kernel with lower transient workspace for memory-constrained hosts.

erica: agree. adding an estimator to picker is medium-effort. for now, canary with bigger blocks + aggressive_reuse should show if compaction is the culprit. if p50 drops and OOMs go away, we can tune further.

miko: canary started. I'll post results in ~30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — if canary looks good, we should ship a targeted rollback for fused_kv_v2 auto-prefer change and add picker perf label until estimator exists.

erica: noted. also create an alert for compaction_time > 2s per minute so we catch regressions earlier.

miko: result snapshot (30m):
```
canary: p50 down 9% vs regression run, compaction_runs=1.1K (vs 9.8K), compaction_time_ms=540, cuda_ooms=0, mem_headroom_avg=220MB
```

oliver: nice! seems block bump + reuse flag did it. next steps: make picker workspace estimator and a kernel metadata field `estimated_transient_workspace_bytes`.

erica: filing a short RFC for picker estimator + allocator override API. linking notes here when done.

miko: RFC draft: https://intranet.redwood/rfc/paged-attn-blockmap-2026 (WIP)

erica: great work. closing loop once RFC and tests land. :white_check_mark:
